links.comparator_used: Expert raters' agreement with each other, plus frontier LLM judges (GPT-6.1 Sol, Claude Opus 5.5), with agreement against expert labels as the main outcome
links.outcome: Plain agreement with the expert label across six tasks from five clinical benchmarks
links.effect: Jev averaged 64.7% agreement over six tasks. On 3,614 matched units it averaged 66.1% vs 65.0% for Opus and 60.7% for Sol, and was non-inferior to both on four of six tasks. Jev judged the whole pool in 17 minutes for US$1.46, at 1/34 of Sol's cost and 1/152 of Opus's per judgment.
links.tradeoff: Omissions were hard to catch. At the same false-alarm rate, Jev missed 55.6% of planted omissions and Opus 48.1%, and Opus caught 8.8 points more planted errors overall. Expert oversight is still needed for omissions and clinical documents.
links.quote: On 3,614 matched units it averaged 66.1%, against 65.0% for Opus and 60.7% for Sol, and it was non-inferior to both on four of six tasks.

links.outcome: Number of errors found when human reviewers audit the judge's least-sure answers first
links.effect: Reviewing Jev's least-sure answers first found 1.4 times the errors of a random audit; a preset cutoff held its false-alarm rate on fresh planted-error answers.
links.tradeoff: The review-prioritisation result came from simulation, not live deployment. Omissions remained hard to detect.
links.quote: A preset cutoff held its false-alarm rate on fresh planted-error answers, and in simulation, reviewing Jev’s least-sure answers first found 1.4 times the errors of a random audit.
